findings.issue: Raw JSON.parse used instead of safeJsonParse — policy violation per security-patterns.md §2 (prototype-pollution guard). Runtime-safe on Node 20+, but violates project standard.
findings.recommendation: Replace with safeJsonParse + sentinel fallback for parseError categorization.
findings.evidenceNote: Applied fix; 13/13 tests pass including new __proto__/top-level-array rejection test.

findings.issue: os.homedir() not validated against HOME/USERPROFILE hijacking.
findings.recommendation: Theoretical Tier-0 concern; if HOME is hijacked, attacker controls settings.json directly anyway.
findings.evidenceNote: Static inference only; no exploit path demonstrated.
findings.dismissReason: Tier 0 + threat model — dismissed as acceptable risk.

findings.issue: os.tmpdir() without per-user isolation in test.
findings.recommendation: Per-user isolation for dev-only test code.
findings.evidenceNote: Matches project-wide test convention (multiple other test files use identical pattern).
findings.dismissReason: Aligned with existing project test convention; consistency > micro-hardening for dev-only code.

findings.issue: Version compat row claims '2.18.0+' but package.json is 2.17.5.
findings.evidenceNote: Intentional per task spec; will be accurate at release time.

findings.issue: checkMcpScopes() called only in main(), not deepAudit().
findings.recommendation: Deep audit is structural-only by design; MCP scope drift is runtime. Accept as design intent.
findings.evidenceNote: Code flow analysis confirms deepAudit() runs independently.

enforcementGaps.rule: security-patterns.md §2: Use safeJsonParse() instead of raw JSON.parse()
enforcementGaps.rootCause: NO_ENFORCEMENT — no standards-gate check for JSON.parse in new code.
enforcementGaps.resolution: FIXED in-review. Future: add lint rule or standards check.
